summary: Control-plane request latency and intermittent timeouts due to on-prem DNS forwarder TTL drift and negative-cache retention
summary_long: Customers on Acera Health private deployment reported periodic control-plane API requests experiencing 5-10s latency spikes and occasional 504s. Investigation pointed to stale DNS answers being served by an on-prem DNS forwarder with aggressive negative/positive TTL skew, causing the Redwood control plane to continue routing requests to an unreachable (cached) NAT egress path for ~12 minutes.
description:
Issue summary:
- Control-plane control APIs for Acera Health (private deployment) intermittently returned high latency and occasional 504s between 2026-03-09 22:10 UTC and 2026-03-11 04:30 UTC.
- Customers reported model request retries and degraded streaming stability.

Impact:
- Affected tenant: Acera Health (private). Approximately 12% of control-plane requests during windows experienced >5s latency; 1.3% returned 504.
- Application-facing token issuance and route resolution were delayed, causing downstream model-serving requests to hit fallback/ejected backends.

Environment:
- Private deployment in us-east connected via customer-managed VPN + on-prem DNS forwarder
- Redwood control-plane endpoints: control.acera.redwood-inference.internal (resolved via customer forwarder)
- Customer reported they run a DNS forwarder that conditionally forwards to their internal resolvers and upstream public resolvers with custom TTL handling.
steps_to_reproduce: Trigger control-plane list-models call repeatedly from within customer VPC while toggling their internal resolver to return NXDOMAIN for a temporary internal hostname (simulated)
Observe control-plane health-checks and route-resolve latency in the Redwood Console for the tenant
Capture DNS answers from customer's forwarder and from public resolver to compare TTLs and negative TTL behaviour
logs_and_artifacts: flow-logs: s3://redwood-support/acera/flowlogs/2026-03-10_flow.log -> shows identical queries answered by forwarder at t=22:12 and t=22:18 with cached IP and TTL zero returned
tcpdump: /support-drops/acera/tcpdump_controlplane.cap -> shows repeated SYNs to old egress IPs with successful 3-way but no application response
dig-output.txt: control.acera.redwood-inference.internal @10.0.0.2 -> shows TTL 7200 at 22:10, TTL 0 (SOA negative caching) at 22:14
redwood-console-trace: trace_id=rdw-ctl-115879-0001 -> shows DNS_resolve step 9.2s at 2026-03-10T22:14:03Z
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: transient NAT gateway outages. Flow logs showed egress IPs reachable, so not NAT outage.

Observed DNS answers from the customer forwarder had inconsistent TTLs: positive answers returned long TTLs (2h) but when the internal resolver returned NXDOMAIN for certain control-plane helper hostnames the forwarder persisted a negative cache entry with a 12 minute retention and then continued to return the negative entry to us even after the internal resolver recovered.

Control-plane repeatedly attempted to resolve service-relevant hostnames which returned (via the forwarder) a stale CNAME chain during rolling network experiments. The control-plane's resolver cached the forwarded negative responses which delayed fallback to alternate routing policy.
Correlation between DNS negative cache windows and latency spikes is strong (Pearson r=0.82 over event windows).
customer_communication: 2026-03-10 22:30 - Asha Patel (Support): Notified customer of observed DNS negative caching. Requested config dump and forwarder logs.
2026-03-10 23:05 - Acera network team (Maria Gomez): Provided dnsmasq/infoblox configs. Confirmed they have an explicit 'min-ttl' policy and custom NXDOMAIN caching script.
2026-03-11 01:15 - Derek Nguyen (Eng): Suggested temporary change to disable negative caching and add conditional forward for control.acera.redwood-inference.internal -> 10.0.0.11 internal resolver.
2026-03-11 02:40 - Maria Gomez (Acera): Applied workaround and confirmed improved latency metrics; requested timeline for permanent fix.
correlation_and_root_cause: Root cause: Customer on-prem DNS forwarder applied a negative-caching policy that created a multi-minute negative cache for internal control-plane helper hostnames after a transient internal resolver outage. The forwarder continued returning those negative answers to the Redwood control plane, which then cached the negative responses for the control-plane process and did not immediately failover to alternate routing. Result: control-plane route resolution delays and fallback triggering causing high latency and some 504s.
workarounds_and_mitigation: Applied temporary customer-side workaround at 2026-03-11 02:40: disable NXDOMAIN negative caching and reduce min-ttl to 30s for control.*.redwood-inference.internal zone
Redwood support pushed a short-lived control-plane resolver override for the tenant to ignore negative answers for 120s while the forwarding policy was corrected (rolled back 2026-03-12 08:00)
resolution: Customer disabled negative-caching and reduced min-ttl for the control-plane domain. Redwood applied a tenant-scoped resolver safety patch to ignore NXDOMAINs for critical control-plane helper names for a 2-minute window while the customer remediation completed. Post-fix monitoring shows latency restored to baseline: <1% requests >2s and 0.1% 504s in the 24h after remediation.
postmortem_actions: Docs: Add guidance to Private Deploy runbooks about on-prem forwarder negative caching behavior and recommended TTLs for control-plane zones
Product: Implement resolver-configurable per-tenant negative-cache-ignore list (EPIC created INT-402)
SRE: Add an alert for sustained DNS NXDOMAIN rate >20% for a tenant over 5m (create alert rule)
comments: 2026-03-10 22:45 - Derek Nguyen: I see the same negative TTLs in their forwarder logs. Customer's infoblox has a 'nx-cache-min' scripted value set to 720 seconds. That will keep NXDOMAINs around and is the likely cause.
2026-03-11 00:12 - SRE (Lena Ortiz): Added temporary grafana panel to show per-tenant NXDOMAIN ratio and TTL anomalies.
2026-03-11 02:55 - Maria Gomez (Acera): Confirmed disabling NX cache. Latencies dropped immediately in our tests. Will pursue permanent config change with infra team.
2026-03-12 07:20 - Derek Nguyen: Rolled back tenant-scoped resolver override. Monitoring nominal.
notes: This ticket highlights an operational mismatch between customer DNS policies and Redwood control-plane resolver assumptions. Recommend adding explicit preflight checks for TTL/negative-cache behavior during Private deployment onboarding.
